evals.prompt: Here is my placement for a small buck + module board (evals/files/placement_bad.json). Is it ready to push to the EDA tool?
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/placement_check.py on the file, reports ERROR 6 / WARN 5 with the overlaps, the edge and keep-out violations and the buck input cap that is 7.6 mm from U2, says the placement is not ready, and proposes concrete moves.
assertions: placement_check.py was actually run (its SUMMARY line is quoted)
the answer says the placement is NOT ready (ERROR > 0)
the C3 -> U2 distance violation is named with the buck hot-loop reason
no coordinates are presented as final while ERROR > 0

evals.prompt: How many 0.3 mm vias do I need to carry 5 A from the top layer to an inner plane? 1.6 mm board, 20 um plating.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/pcbcalc.py via-current (about 0.53 A per via at 10 C rise with 0.7 derating), concludes about 10 vias (>= 9.4) for 10 C rise, states the assumptions and limits, and mentions the plane width / copper weight as the next weakest element.
assertions: pcbcalc.py via-current was run rather than a rule of thumb
the per-via figure is between 0.45 and 0.65 A and the count is between 8 and 12
assumptions (temperature rise, plating, derating) are stated

evals.prompt: Before I order: check the fabrication files in evals/files/board_bad against the netlist evals/files/board_bad.ipc.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/gerber_check.py netcheck, reports one short (net A to net B at R1) and one open (net A: missing via between the top copper and U1-1 on the bottom), and says the files must not be ordered as they are.
assertions: both the short between A and B and the open on A are reported
the answer advises against ordering these files

evals.prompt: Review this note from my layout: 'The 24 V motor phase OUT1A is 0.25 mm wide for 6 mm and carries 1.5 A RMS.' Give me the finding.
evals.expected_output: One finding in the skill format: severity (Major), title, evidence with the pcbcalc trace-width result for 1.5 A on 1 oz outer copper (about 0.53 mm at 10 C rise, 0.35 mm at 20 C), impact, fix, confidence.
assertions: the finding uses the [Severity] title / Evidence / Impact / Fix / Confidence structure
the required width comes from pcbcalc.py trace-width, not from memory
severity is not Critical for a fixable width issue

evals.prompt: I placed all parts of my EasyEDA Pro board with a script. Now I changed one resistor in the schematic. Can I just run Import Changes on the PCB?
evals.expected_output: Warns that on a script-placed board importChanges proposes to remove and re-add every part (placement and routing lost), and describes the part-swap method instead: new device at the old position with the old unique id, pad nets copied by pad number, netlist comparison afterwards.
assertions: the answer says not to apply importChanges on that board and why
the part-swap procedure from references/easyeda_pro_api.md is given
a netlist comparison after the edit is required
